memory_update.text: FORM should remain a high-priority underfollowed candidate for the advanced-packaging/HBM-test node because company materials directly tie its probe cards to HBM, known-good-die, interposer, and advanced-packaging test flows.

ONTO should remain in the discovery lane as a process-control and inspection/metrology candidate for AI-related advanced packaging, with later-layer work focused on revenue purity and HBM customer evidence.
COHU is a lower-attention HBM inspection/test automation candidate; survival to later layers depends on proving that the Neon HBM platform is commercially material.

ACMR is a speculative-shadow candidate for advanced-packaging wet processing, TSV, and plating exposure; the key gap is whether this maps to meaningful AI/HBM customer demand rather than generic semiconductor capex.

summary: Expanded the underfollowed universe for the advanced-packaging/HBM-test chokepoint. The strongest Layer 1B candidates are not the obvious GPU or mega-cap equipment leaders, but niche public suppliers tied to probe cards, HBM inspection/metrology, semiconductor test automation, and wet-processing/electroplating steps used in TSV, wafer-level packaging, and advanced interconnect formation. These companies remain hypotheses for later layers because revenue purity, customer concentration, backlog durability, and AI/HBM-specific revenue disclosure still need verification.
